hero.title: Understand the connections. Put the methods to work.
hero.lede: Explore three complementary methods, see why they connect, and use them to frame your own problem.
hero.thesis: A problem map sets boundaries, an evidence chain tests claims, and an action loop brings new information.

frameworks.when: Entering an unfamiliar or poorly defined problem

contentUnits.label: Unit 1
contentUnits.title: Frame the problem
contentUnits.core: Define the scope before choosing an action.
takeaways: Make constraints and success criteria explicit.

conclusions.title: Boundary before action
conclusions.summary: A map helps identify which information is relevant.
points: Record what belongs inside the problem.

contentUnits.label: Unit 2
contentUnits.title: Test the claim
contentUnits.core: Observations and explanations are not the same thing.

conclusions.title: Evidence is not automatic proof
conclusions.summary: One observation may allow more than one explanation.
points: Separate what was observed from what it might mean.
Seek evidence that could challenge the current claim.

contentUnits.label: Unit 3
contentUnits.title: Learn through action
contentUnits.core: A small test should produce information that can change the next decision.
takeaways: Test an important assumption at low cost.
Compare results with predictions before scaling.

conclusions.title: Feed results back into thinking
conclusions.summary: Results may update the evidence chain or the problem boundary.
points: Return to the problem map when constraints change.
These methods are not a guarantee of success.

glossary.definition: The scope of the problem being addressed.
glossary.context: The problem map makes the boundary explicit before action.

glossary.definition: Evidence that could challenge a current claim.
glossary.context: The evidence chain uses it to check confidence rather than accept one observation as proof.

glossary.definition: Information from a test used to revise an assumption or next action.
glossary.context: The action loop compares results with predictions and can update earlier thinking.

decisionRules.because: The boundary helps identify relevant information

decisionRules.when: Confidence in a claim is low
decisionRules.because: A single observation should not be treated as proof
Its result can update assumptions and guide the next action

relationships.explanation: Drawing the map makes its boundaries and success criteria usable when the scope is unclear.
Seeking counterevidence is one way to test a weakly supported claim.
A small informative test starts the action loop when discussion is stalled.
Test results provide new observations for the evidence chain.
Changed constraints can require revisiting the problem map.
A clear boundary can help focus evidence gathering. This is an analytical connection, not a required sequence stated by the material.

methods.name: Problem map
methods.summary: Make boundaries, stakeholders, constraints and success criteria explicit.
methods.problem: An unclear problem scope makes relevant information difficult to identify.
methods.when: Entering an unfamiliar or poorly defined problem
prerequisites: A problem and an observable desired result can be described.
limitations: The source gives no universal success guarantee or quantitative threshold.
Order and suitability depend on the problem and available evidence.
methods.rationale: An explicit boundary helps decide which information is relevant.

steps.action: Record the problem boundary and stakeholders.
steps.output: An explicit scope and stakeholder list.
steps.check: Check whether each listed item belongs to the scope.

steps.action: Record constraints and an observable success criterion.
steps.check: Check that the criterion can be observed.

successChecks: Boundary, stakeholders, constraints and observable success criterion are explicit.

sources.quote: Before choosing an action, record the problem boundary, stakeholders, constraints and an observable success criterion.
These methods are complementary tools, not a guarantee of success.

methods.name: Evidence chain
methods.summary: Connect conclusions to observations and competing explanations.
methods.problem: A claim has weak support or several possible explanations.
methods.when: Judging whether a claim is well supported
prerequisites: A claim and relevant observations are available for examination.
limitations: The source gives no universal success guarantee or quantitative threshold.
Order and suitability depend on the problem and available evidence.
methods.rationale: A single observation should not be treated as proof.

steps.output: A distinction between observed facts and interpretations.
steps.check: Check that interpretations are not presented as direct observations.
Do not treat one observation as proof; the source gives no numeric evidence threshold.

successChecks: Observations and interpretations are separate; competing explanations were considered.

sources.quote: Separate observations from explanations. Link conclusions to observations and look for competing explanations.
These methods are complementary tools, not a guarantee of success.

methods.name: Action loop
methods.summary: Test an assumption, compare prediction and outcome, then revise.
methods.problem: Discussion stalls without information to guide a decision.
methods.when: Turning understanding into a small informative action
prerequisites: An important assumption can be tested at small scale.
limitations: The source gives no universal success guarantee or quantitative threshold.
Order and suitability depend on the problem and available evidence.
methods.rationale: A test can produce new information and change the next decision.

steps.action: Choose a small, low-cost test of an important assumption.
steps.output: An informative test and its result.
steps.check: Check whether the test produces new information.

steps.action: Compare the result with the prediction and revise before scaling.
steps.output: A revised assumption or next decision.
steps.check: Use changed constraints to revisit the problem map where needed.

successChecks: A test result was compared with a prediction before scaling.

sources.quote: Choose a small, low-cost test of an important assumption, compare its result with your prediction, and revise the assumption before scaling the action.
